analysis.title: Asia Open - Taking cover
key_insights: Risk-off tone across asset classes at the start of the week. Flows rotated back into USTs after last week's selloff in rates, which began with a hotter-than-expected CPI print. SPX fell nearly 2% with every sector lower except consumer staples.

The continued unwind of AI picks and shovels pushed SPX down 2% and NDX down 2.7%. More than 380 SPX constituents closed lower, and the desk notes liquidity is thinning ahead of the US holiday season.
Nvidia fell about 4% after a CNBC report that the company is not considering reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO. The desk ties the move to mounting calls and a broad-based petition for his return.
Nvidia earnings are the main event of the week. The options market prices the session after the print at SPX 1.05% and QQQ 1.77%.
Index vols were bid, with Jan ATM SPX +0.2v, QQQ +0.65v and IWM +0.2v. Customer flow was two-way but skewed toward buying options in SPX and QQQ, with QQQ activity concentrated in 1-2 week expiries.

Fed Chair Warsh gave little guidance and spoke about AI. He said the Fed's role is neither advocacy nor opposition, and that after significant capital investment and stock market gains, expected returns could turn down and equity valuations could fall.
Cleveland Fed President Hammack reiterated a preference for slow, steady rate hikes. The 5y led the Treasury rally, down 2bps on the day, and a light US data calendar puts Fedspeak in focus.

The dollar firmed, with DXY up 0.18% to 103.59, as equity weakness was met with inflows into USTs and the dollar. Over the past week USD saw net outflows because bank and real-money selling outweighed leveraged buying.
CAD weakened about 0.2% after October headline CPI rose 0.2% MoM and 3.1% YoY, both below consensus. Citi economists expect the BoC to hold rates in December.

Brent fell 3.5% despite fresh Middle East tensions and a third US carrier strike group arriving in the region. The desk says participation is light versus the 10-day average and the market is leaning on the IEA's view that supply exceeded demand last week for the first time since the war began.
Gold fell as much as 1.3% to near $3,830/oz, its lowest level since October 2025, before paring losses. It is trading firmly below $4,000.

USDBRL reached a new cycle high of 5.79 as BRL weakened 2.3%. The market is focused on Brazil's deteriorating fiscal narrative and uncertainty over Lula's new cabinet. Exporters have been timid in selling USD, and desk flows are led by offshore real-money accounts and CTAs.

Data ahead: RBA minutes (00:30 GMT), NZ 2y inflation expectations (02:00 GMT), UK labor data (07:00 GMT) and Singapore NODX. Citi expects the RBA minutes to show two-sided risks but a case for waiting.
A strong UK labor report, especially an unexpected pickup in average wages, would strengthen the case for a December BoE hike. Citi says Wednesday's UK inflation print will matter more.

market_movers.rationale: Shares fell about 4% after a CNBC report that the company is not considering reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO. Earnings on Tuesday are the week's premier event, with the options market pricing the post-earnings session at SPX 1.05% and QQQ 1.77%.

earnings_insights: Nvidia reports Tuesday. No EPS or revenue figures are given. The options market prices the trading session after the print at SPX 1.05% and QQQ 1.77% (market-implied moves, not a consensus estimate).
Citi Equities holds a client Q&A call ahead of NVDA earnings at 13:30 GMT / 08:30 ET.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Below consensus. CAD weakened roughly 0.2% and Citi economists still expect the BoC to hold in December.
Below consensus, supporting an unchanged BoC rate path in December.
The print started last week's sharp repricing in USTs. Rates partially retraced on Monday.
Citi economists expect wages to moderate, with ex-bonus wages at 3.6% and private earnings at 3%. An unexpected pickup would support a December BoE hike.
Citi economists forecast growth could slow from a prior 68.40%.
Up 0.18% on the day, supported by flight-to-quality flows into USD and USTs.
